mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day period of stable rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) crosses above 2% for the first time in a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to turn negative as investors anticipate rate hikes.
regime_hint: early signs of price pressure in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained CPIAUCSL > 2% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by declining industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a labor market dislocation, which tends to weigh on equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 10% while INDPRO falls by more than 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (Rank IC < 0.05) when the PAYEMS-INDPRO interaction is present.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.5% of the prior month's level signals renewed consumer confidence and supports a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite 3 consecutive months of HOUST growth > 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls for three consecutive months below its 12-month moving average, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO in a downward trend for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 30-day average (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a short-term positive S&P 20-day forward return as market anticipates further economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite UNRATE continuing to decline for 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling FEDFUNDS accompanied by rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive as the central bank is likely to pause or reverse rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases while CPIAUCSL increases over the same horizon
regime_hint: conflicting signals of easing inflation and tightening credit
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.05) when the interaction pattern is present.

mechanism_narrative: When the 5-day moving average of daily S&P 500 volatility exceeds 1.8%, the 20-day forward return is expected to be negative, reflecting risk aversion in the face of elevated uncertainty.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05) when volatility is elevated.
